hints.title: Dual Round-Trip Traversal Obstacle
hints.text: Traversing from (0, 0) to (N-1, N-1) and back to pick up cherries cannot be done sequentially because first-path choices alter available cherries. How can stepping two walkers simultaneously from (0, 0) synchronize cherry pickup?

hints.title: Simultaneous Step-Count Invariant
hints.text: When both walkers take k steps, r1 + c1 = k and r2 + c2 = k. They collect cherries at (r1, c1) and (r2, c2), taking the cell cherry only once if r1 == r2.

hints.title: 2D State Step Rolling Procedure
hints.text: Represent states by step count k and row coordinates r1, r2. At each step, both walkers move right or down (4 transitions). Update transitions where neither walker lands on a thorn (-1). If both land on the same cell, add cherry count once, otherwise add both. Return 0 if the destination is unreachable.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Iterates through 2N steps with N x N state transitions per step.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Solving two paths sequentially fails greedily because the optimal first path can starve the return path.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing only previous step matrix requires O(N^2) space instead of O(N^3).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Converting a round-trip path into two simultaneous forward paths.
